coverage_note: 00:57-01:10 is Medi talking to a voice assistant, not part of the lesson. 06:01-06:34: Amal's lines are garbled ('تشرب ليون' is probably a date question). 07:55: 'ألأ' is a2al (أقل) in Levantine sound, so it is pronunciation (S4) and not a slip; Amal's 08:05 'أقل' only spells it out. 13:58 and 14:03 are garbled ('شفياني هاي', 'elbowss are then' is probably el-buza...). 25:21: Amal's 'باب سيت' and Medi's Latin 'babset' (25:30) are ببسط; echo: babset = ببسط. 27:05 غادة for غابة and 29:16 قابة for غابة are mishearing or pronunciation (S4), not written as rows. 1:01:53: her 'قلت انتين' notes ثنتين vs تنتين, which is pronunciation. 1:06:21: زغار -> رخاص looks like his own fix ('No, small') at the same time as her الرخص; not written. 1:10:34 'مع الشوق بك' is unclear, maybe the engine; not written. Several English-only stretches: 03:12-03:24, 15:35-16:50, 33:08-34:28, 36:19-37:46, 52:46-53:33. Per GR-19, chat lines were used only as context.

rows.why: بوجع is the I-form (I hurt someone); the stomach is what hurts, so it should be بيوجع(ني). Her question was about فمي (mouth), which he had already fixed himself.

rows.medi_said: لازم أشتري نانا أك-- uh, ن-نانا.
rows.why: She had just asked 'بتعرف نعنع؟'; he said نانا (not her word), and she recast نعنع طازة.

rows.proposed_rule: To say someone got better (a change of state), use saar + adjective: khatibti saarat a7san
rows.why: He meant she got better; Amal supplied صارت, and he took it ('Became better, yeah'). The bare sentence is not ungrammatical, so confidence is low.

rows.amal_said: أطلب؟ ... You're gonna ask of her? ... or order for her?
rows.why: Asking someone for something takes ba6lob min (sheet: 'Ana ba6lob min'); she questioned it and he fixed it to أطلب منها.
In idafa the first word takes no el-, and she wanted the plural كلمات; he repeated الكلمات الطبيعات at 08:39 and she recast كلمات الطبيعة.

rows.amal_said: كلمات الطبيعة. ... لا، طبيعة just nature. Don't have plural of nature.
rows.why: He invented a plural طبيعات; she said nature has no plural.
Asked for hidden-feminine nature words, he offered قارة (continent); she answered أرض right away. This may be her giving the answer rather than a fix.
He said he forgot the word, and she supplied هواء.
'My favorite' on its own needs 3indi; she prompted 'شو بزيد؟' and then finished it herself.
A definite noun + adjective needs el- on both; she recast البوظة الحلوة.

rows.amal_said: Okay, so بوظة's feminine. Would it be مفضلة؟ - Mm-hmm. ... I said it after you as well.
rows.why: مفضل follows the feminine noun بوظة, so it must be مفضلة; she confirmed this and said she had said it after him (bare بوظة without el- also repeated).

rows.medi_said: الـ مفضل. No. مفضل الـ. الـ مفضل الـ.
rows.why: مفضل is an adjective after the noun; she said No three times, and he rebuilt it as بوظتي المفضلة.

rows.amal_said: No. This is my favorite. يعني my favorite's on its own, so we use the new one
rows.why: 'X are my favorite' standing alone needs el-X el-mufaddal 3indi, not a possessive ending; she said No.

rows.medi_said: المفضل is-- جبال is masculine, right?
rows.why: The adjective must agree with the plural جبال; she pointed out it is plural, and he said المفضلين.
Asked for one mountain, he gave the plural; she gave the singular جبل.

rows.amal_said: Wow, you remember many words. So beach is
rows.why: He used the formal (MSA) شاطئ; she prompted 'So beach is' and he said شط, her word (sheet: 'beach | Sha66 | شط'). It may only be quizzing.

rows.medi_said: Um, the other lake. So بحيرة تاني.
rows.why: 'The other' needs el-noun el-taani, with feminine تانية; she prompted 'The other lake' and recast البحيرة الثانية after his half-fix.
شط/شاطئ is masculine, so it takes هذا; she said هذا and he repeated it.

rows.right: بتحبي (my reader's reading, from her chat)
rows.why: Her typed version addresses a woman (bet7ebbi), and he used the masculine you-form; the chat alone is not a correction.

rows.amal_said: أنا بروح to. ... بروح عليها. I go to.
rows.why: 'Go to' takes 3ala with the ending (sheet: 'i go to | Ana baru7 3ala'), not an ending on the verb; she gave بروح عليها.

The numbers 3-10 take a plural noun; she prompted, and her chat gives wara2aat.

rows.amal_said: What would it means? ... سؤالي الأخير ... Or آخر سؤال إلي.

Feminine لعبة keeps its -t before the possessive ending; she recast لعبتي (he then fixed هذه and الأولى himself).
